# Chromium LevelDB fixtures

These closed databases were generated by `generate.cc`, linked against
Chromium's LevelDB revision `7ee830d02b623e8ffe0b95d59a74db1e58da04c5`.
The generator checks every entry against the native engine's iterator before
closing each database. Rust tests independently reconstruct the expected data.

- `chromium/randomized-long-db`: the 100,000-operation `Harness.RandomizedLongDB`
  workload, fixed seed 301, binary and empty keys, duplicate-key updates,
  multiple live SSTs, and the final WAL not yet converted into an SST.
- `chromium/recovery`: SSTs plus a fragmented WAL with updates, deletes, binary
  and empty keys/values, and a 120,000-byte replacement value.

The native fixtures use uncompressed tables. The Rust ports exercise both
uncompressed and Snappy-compressed data/index blocks, independently of whether
the host has a C++ Snappy library installed. Cargo tests read the checked-in
fixtures directly; they need no C++ compiler, downloads, or fixture generation.

To regenerate, run from the repository root with an empty scratch directory:

```sh
git clone https://chromium.googlesource.com/external/leveldb /tmp/moli-leveldb-fixture-source
git -C /tmp/moli-leveldb-fixture-source checkout 7ee830d02b623e8ffe0b95d59a74db1e58da04c5
cmake -S /tmp/moli-leveldb-fixture-source -B /tmp/moli-leveldb-fixture-build \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DLEVELDB_BUILD_TESTS=OFF \
  -DLEVELDB_BUILD_BENCHMARKS=OFF -DLEVELDB_INSTALL=OFF
cmake --build /tmp/moli-leveldb-fixture-build
c++ -std=c++17 -O2 moli-leveldb-parser/tests/fixtures/generate.cc \
  -I/tmp/moli-leveldb-fixture-source/include -I/tmp/moli-leveldb-fixture-source \
  /tmp/moli-leveldb-fixture-build/libleveldb.a -pthread \
  -o /tmp/moli-leveldb-fixture-generator
/tmp/moli-leveldb-fixture-generator /tmp/moli-leveldb-fixtures
```

If CMake detects optional native Snappy, CRC32C or Zstd libraries, link those as
well. Inspect the generated contents before replacing `chromium/`. Background
compaction can change file numbers/layout between runs; the expected logical
contents are fixed. `SHA256SUMS` records the checked-in files, not an assertion
that regenerated database files must be byte-for-byte identical.

See [TESTS.md](../../TESTS.md) for upstream sources and port coverage and
[LICENSE-LevelDB](../../LICENSE-LevelDB) for the upstream license.
